_README: HARNESS FIXTURE — canon deal facts for test/build-memo.mjs. Not shipped to seats; the plugin's own runtime data lives in credit-memo-agent/assets/. Data is real: identity + deal + covenants pulled from the BankingGPT nCino sandbox (Account 001bb00001DLtRMAA1); financial spread from Boom file 01f7b073 (completed FY2024 vs FY2023, US$). This canon is an EARLIER vintage than assets/boom-ratios.json — it models Piedmont at ~breakeven EBITDA, so EBITDA-based ratios (leverage, FCCR) compute to NS; render NS/— and move on, never fabricate. The harness exercises the renderer, not data currency.

borrower.name: Piedmont Precision Components, Inc.
borrower.profile: Privately held precision-machining manufacturer (founded 1998) producing high-tolerance components for aerospace, defense, and medical-device end markets. ~110,000 sq ft, 182 employees, AS9100D / ISO 13485 certified.

exposureSummary._note: Acme Bank exposure. Existing = the $5.0M booked WC revolver ($4.25M drawn, serviced in AFS). Proposed = $7.5M revolver (after +$2.5M increase) + $5.0M new Equipment TL = $12.5M.

spread._note: Boom spread, file 01f7b073 (completed). Two REAL annual periods only (FY2023, FY2024); US$. adjusted_ebitda = operating_profit + D&A → ~breakeven in FY2024 (-$19K), so leverage/FCCR compute to NS. net_income = continuing operations, net of tax. Discontinued operation nearly wound down (FY24 residual -$111K vs FY23 -$7.24M).

covenants.name: Minimum Debt Service Coverage
covenants.definition: (EBITDA − unfinanced CapEx − cash taxes − distributions) / (interest + scheduled principal).
covenants._note: nCino-reported actual 1.42x vs 1.25x trigger = ~13.6% cushion. Binding constraint.

industryOutlook.outlook: Stable-to-improving. Commercial aerospace build-rate recovery and sustained defense spending support high-tolerance machining demand; reshoring of precision supply chains is a tailwind for AS9100D/ISO-13485 shops.

narratives.execSummary: Piedmont Precision Components seeks a $5.0M equipment term loan to fund three Mazak INTEGREX multi-tasking CNC machines, alongside a $2.5M increase & renewal of its existing $5.0M working-capital revolver (to $7.5M). The borrower is a 26-year aerospace/defense precision machinist (AS9100D / ISO 13485) with a diversified blue-chip customer base and a multi-year contracted backlog. FY2025 revenue reached $64.5M (+7.5% YoY), but adjusted EBITDA margin softened to ~7.9% ($5.1M) on elevated labor and new-program qualification costs, lifting leverage to ~3.9x (~4.9x pro forma). Liquidity ($8.2M) and DSC (1.42x) remain inside covenant, and the unlimited guaranty of principal Margaret Holloway provides additional support. Recommended for approval at a 5 — Pass/Watch risk rating, with close monitoring of the margin trend.
narratives.requestDetails:
Purpose. $5.0M new-money equipment term loan (7-year, monthly amortization) to acquire three Mazak INTEGREX i-450 multi-tasking CNC centers supporting a newly awarded defense program. Concurrently, the existing $5.0M working-capital revolver is increased by $2.5M to $7.5M and renewed for 364 days.

Sources & Uses. Uses: $5.0M equipment + $2.5M incremental working capital = $7.5M new money. Sources: $5.0M Acme Bank equipment term loan + $2.5M revolver increase.
narratives.borrowerDescription: Founded in 1998 and headquartered in Greensboro, NC, Piedmont Precision Components is a privately held precision-machining manufacturer producing high-tolerance components for aerospace, defense, and medical-device end markets. The company operates a ~110,000 sq ft facility with 182 employees and holds AS9100D and ISO 13485 certifications. Ownership rests with founder-CEO Margaret Holloway, who provides a personal guaranty.
narratives.strengthsRisks:
Strengths. Long-tenured (since 2009) relationship; AS9100D/ISO 13485 certifications create high customer switching costs; multi-year contracted backlog; tangible collateral coverage from late-model CNC equipment; full guaranty of the principal.

Risks & Mitigants. EBITDA margin softened to ~7.9% in FY2025 (from ~11% in FY2023) on new-program ramp and labor inflation, lifting leverage to ~3.9x (mitigant: contracted price escalators and backlog conversion in FY2026); customer concentration in defense primes (mitigant: diversified program mix, long program lifecycles); equipment-purchase execution risk (mitigant: established Mazak platform, vendor install support).
narratives.managementOwnership: Margaret Holloway (founder, President & CEO; 100% owner) leads a stable senior team averaging 12+ years of tenure. No management changes occurred during the review period. Ms. Holloway provides an unlimited personal guaranty of the facilities.
narratives.financialCommentary: FY2025 revenue of $64.5M grew ~7.5% year-over-year, but profitability softened: gross margin compressed to ~21.6% and adjusted EBITDA margin declined to ~7.9% ($5.1M, from ~9.7% in FY2024) on elevated direct labor, training, and first-article qualification costs ahead of full-rate production. Total funded debt of $20.2M (pro forma $25.2M including the $5.0M equipment loan) puts leverage at ~3.9x EBITDA (~4.9x pro forma) — elevated for the rating but supported by tangible collateral and a contracted backlog. Management projects EBITDA-margin recovery in FY2026 as the new program reaches full rate and qualification spend rolls off; the margin trajectory is the key monitoring item.
narratives.recommendation:
Recommendation. Approve the $5.0M equipment term loan and the $2.5M increase & renewal of the working-capital revolver (to $7.5M) at a 5 — Pass/Watch risk rating. The credit is supported by tangible collateral, a contracted backlog, the principal's guaranty, and covenant headroom (DSC 1.42x vs 1.25x; liquidity $8.2M vs $5.0M), tempered by softening margins and elevated pro forma leverage.

Conditions & Monitoring. Quarterly financial reporting with covenant compliance certificate; annual field exam of working-capital collateral; first-lien UCC on the financed equipment. Watch item: FY2025 EBITDA-margin recovery toward management plan in FY2026; revisit the risk rating if margin softening continues beyond Q2-2026.
narratives.guarantorProfile: Margaret Holloway provides an unlimited continuing guaranty of the Piedmont facilities. As founder and sole shareholder, her interests are fully aligned with the borrower. A current personal financial statement is on file; updated PFS and tax returns are a standard reporting condition.
narratives.globalCashFlow: On a combined basis, borrower operating cash flow plus guarantor liquidity covers pro forma fixed charges. Global debt-service coverage is supported primarily at the operating-company level, with the guaranty providing secondary support. A formal global cash-flow model will be maintained in AFS once the connector lands.
narratives.collateralBlanket: The working-capital line is secured by a first-priority blanket lien on all business assets, including accounts receivable and inventory, supported by a borrowing-base certificate and periodic field exams.
narratives.collateralEquipment: The equipment term loan is secured by a first-priority purchase-money security interest in the three financed Mazak INTEGREX CNC machines, plus the borrower's existing late-model machine tools. Orderly-liquidation coverage is supported by the active secondary market for Mazak multi-tasking equipment.
